title: while Loops and Repeated Execution
learningObjectives: Explain while loops and repeated execution and their execution flow.
Trace condition checks and state changes across iterations.
Select a suitable loop structure for a given problem.
Identify common termination and boundary mistakes.
Apply the loop pattern in an original small program.

understand.concept: A while loop tests its condition before each pass; it may execute zero times. Update loop state so termination can occur.
understand.whyItMatters: while is ideal when repetitions depend on a condition rather than a fixed count.
understand.explain: Trace condition → body → update → condition. Check that the condition eventually becomes false.

examples.title: Count 1 to 5
examples.explanation: Prints five values; the counter advances until the condition fails.

examples.title: Sum 1 through 4
examples.explanation: The accumulator retains the running total.

examples.title: Countdown
examples.explanation: The condition is tested before each countdown pass.

examples.title: Search divisible by 7
examples.explanation: The loop searches until a multiple is found.

examples.title: Validate range
examples.explanation: Repeats while age is outside the allowed range; handle input failures in production.

practise.guidedTask: Trace and annotate each of the five while Loops and Repeated Execution examples. For every iteration, record the relevant variable values, condition result and action. Change one input or bound and predict the new behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ program demonstrating while loops and repeated execution in a practical scenario. Include at least three typical tests, two boundary tests, and one invalid or termination test. Explain how the loop terminates.
hints: Write the stopping condition in plain language.
Trace one normal and one boundary input.
Check whether input extraction can fail.

questions.prompt: When is a while condition tested?
questions.explanation: A while loop is a pre-test loop.
The body may be skipped entirely.

questions.prompt: What helps a counter loop terminate?
options: Updating state toward a false condition
questions.answer: Updating state toward a false condition
questions.explanation: Loop state must eventually make the condition false.
Input can be out of range or fail to parse.
